scope_limitation.statement: The absolute total cannot be reconstructed from the permitted evidence. The scenario's input tuple (roster membership, champion identities, levels, ability ranks, item builds, fight window) for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' is defined in scripts/ (the golden corpus), which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids this oracle from reading. It does not appear anywhere under data/ (grep for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' over the whole export returns nothing; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json contains a different, Practice-Tool corpus).
scope_limitation.consequence: This receipt adjudicates the CHANGE (the 33.0 delta) against the cached wiki text and the quoted formulas, rather than re-deriving 4041.9 from first principles. Both candidate mechanisms consistent with the delta independently favour the new value; that concordance, not a from-scratch total, is the basis of the verdict.

observed_delta.rounding_note: Golden leaves carry one decimal, so the true delta is 33.0 +/- 0.1 and every fitted quantity below inherits that band.

sources_quoted.locator: item 3877 (Bloodsong) -> passives[0] (name 'Spellblade') -> branches[0]; line 83147 of the cached file
sources_quoted.verbatim: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
sources_quoted.reading: {{rd|X|Y}} is the wiki's ranged-difference template: X applies to a melee wielder, Y to a ranged wielder. Expose Weakness therefore amplifies ALL damage the debuffed target takes by 8% (melee holder) or 5% (ranged holder), for 4 s, on a 1.5 s internal cooldown.
Corroborates the melee-first / ranged-second ordering of the template: in every cached instance the first value is the larger melee figure and the second the reduced ranged figure.

sources_quoted.locator: objects -> atoms sourced from 'Bloodsong.passives[0].branches[0]' (atom_ids damage.basic_attack / damage.bonus / damage.on_hit / damage.physical / timing.cooldown)
sources_quoted.reading: The parsed atom independently pins the same six numbers: 10 s Spellblade window, 100% base AD, 4 s Expose Weakness, 8% and 5% amplification, 1.5 s cooldown. The 8/5 pair survives parsing as two distinct percents, i.e. the range-conditional amp is present in the cache, not an artefact of my reading of the raw template.

sources_quoted.verbatim: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.  ||  Non-{{tip|basic damage}} dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame.
sources_quoted.reading: Cap C = 5 stacks, 6% percentage armor reduction per stack, 30% at cap, 6 s stack duration. Black Cleaver contributes no damage row of its own; it can only move a target's health_damage through the armor it shreds.

sources_quoted.verbatim: the established model uses a fixed `0.8·max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesàro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C − C(C−1)/(2h)` for `h ≥ C`; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to ±20% at the extremes. ... **Recommendation:** replace the constant with the closed-form Cesàro mean when a champion module needs exact BC numbers (a candidate P3 item; changing it re-tunes every BC fight in the corpus, so it is not a P2 foundation change).
sources_quoted.reading: The document names the 0.8*max_stacks constant as an APPROXIMATION and the Cesàro mean as the EXACT mean of the capped ramp, and pre-announces that replacing it re-tunes corpus BC fights.

sources_quoted.locator: Section 2.1 and the Section 5 audit table, row 'Resistance mitigation'
sources_quoted.reading: The mitigation operator used below to convert an armor-reduction change into a damage change.

sources_quoted.locator: Section 1.2, item 1 (linearity of expectation, multi-hit abilities)
sources_quoted.verbatim: the mitigation operator `x ↦ x·100/(100+R)` is *linear in raw damage* for a fixed resistance
sources_quoted.reading: Justifies additively decomposing the participant's total health_damage into an amplified sub-total and an unamplified remainder when fitting the Expose Weakness hypothesis.

step_0_identity_check.claim: Verify S3's closed form before using it, rather than trusting the document.
step_0_identity_check.derivation: Stacks over h damaging hits follow the capped ramp min(k, C), k = 1..h. For h >= C the exact arithmetic (Cesàro) mean is (1/h)[ sum_{k=1..C} k + (h−C)·C ] = (1/h)[ C(C+1)/2 + hC − C^2 ] = C − C(C−1)/(2h).
step_0_identity_check.verification: Independently re-derived; matches S3 exactly. At C = 5, h = 10 it gives 5 − 20/20 = 4.0, identical to the legacy constant 0.8 * 5 = 4.0 — which is precisely the '~10 autos' agreement S3 claims. The document's formula is therefore correct as written.
step_0_identity_check.sign_consequence: The exact mean is BELOW the 4.0 constant for every h < 10 and ABOVE it for h > 10. A drop in the damage a target takes therefore requires h < 10 damaging hits in the window — normal for a short coupled roster fight.

hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness.rule: S1/S1c: Expose Weakness = +8% damage taken (melee holder) or +5% (ranged holder), all sources, 4 s.
hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness.bug_shape: The literal `{{rd|8%|5%}}` puts the melee figure first; a reader that takes the first parsed percent applies 8% unconditionally. For a RANGED Bloodsong holder the sourced figure is 5%.
hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness.algebra: Let U be health_damage taken outside the Expose Weakness window and B the unamplified damage inside it. Mitigation is linear in raw damage at fixed resistance (S5), so the amp composes additively: old = U + 1.08·B, new = U + 1.05·B. Subtracting: 0.03·B = 33.0 => B = 1100.0 (+/- 3.3 from the 0.1 rounding band).
hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness.plausibility: A 4 s Expose Weakness window carrying ~28.6% of a participant's incoming damage is unremarkable for a coupled roster fight of roughly 12–15 s. Self-consistent, and the direction (down) is exactly what correcting melee-8% to ranged-5% produces.
hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness.residual_uncertainty: If the scenario's Bloodsong holder is MELEE, 8% is the sourced figure and this hypothesis would instead favour the old value. I cannot see the roster, so this branch is not closed by evidence — only by the observation that a 'first-value-wins' misread is the natural failure mode of `{{rd|8%|5%}}`, and that the correction direction matches.

hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_cesaro.rule: S2 (C = 5 stacks, 6% armor reduction each) + S3 (exact mean C − C(C−1)/(2h), replacing the 0.8·max_stacks = 4.0 constant) + S4 (m(R) = 100/(100+R)).
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_cesaro.algebra: For the physical damage a Black Cleaver carrier deals into armor A, health_damage scales as m(A·(1−r)) = 100/(100 + A(1−r)) with r the fractional armor reduction. Setting new/old = (100 + A(1−r_old)) / (100 + A(1−r_new)) = 0.9919016 with r_old = 0.06·4.0 = 0.24 and r_new = 0.06·(5 − 10/h), and solving for A:
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_cesaro.plausibility: h = 8 damaging hits against ~93 armor is a textbook level-18 target and reproduces the observed 0.81% drop essentially exactly (all-physical limit); h = 7 against ~42 armor also fits. h = 9 requires an absurd 1768 armor and is excluded. So the delta sits comfortably inside the range the exact Cesàro mean produces for a short fight.
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_cesaro.note: The solve assumes the participant's incoming damage is predominantly physical and shredded by a single Black Cleaver; a mixed-damage roster shifts the implied armor upward but not the sign.

why_the_two_hypotheses_agree_on_the_verd: Hypothesis A: the cached wiki text (S1) and its parsed atom (S1c) both carry 8% AND 5% as range-conditional alternatives. Only one of them is right for a given holder, and 8% — the first-listed, melee value — is the one a naive reader defaults to. The correction direction (8% -> 5%, damage down) matches the observed sign, and the fit is exact and self-consistent.

Hypothesis B: the engine's own foundations document (S3) labels the 0.8·max_stacks constant an APPROXIMATION and names the Cesàro mean C − C(C−1)/(2h) as the EXACT mean of the capped ramp defined by S2 — an identity I re-derived independently and confirmed. Replacing an admitted approximation with the verified exact mean makes the post-change number the more source-faithful one, and S3 explicitly predicts such a replacement 're-tunes every BC fight in the corpus', which is what a leaf like this one is.

Both mechanisms are consistent with the 33.0 drop, and under BOTH the post-change value is the one the sources support. No mechanism I could construct from the permitted evidence makes 4074.9 the sourced value while 4041.9 is not.

arithmetic_alternatives_considered_and_l.comment: Both are arithmetically consistent with a 33.0 delta and cannot be excluded without the scenario tuple. Neither would overturn the verdict: removing an amp that the target's wielder does not grant, or that the fight window does not cover, also moves the leaf toward the sourced value.

independent_computation.what_would_close_this_conclusively: Sight of the scenario's roster (which participant carries Bloodsong and whether that champion is melee or ranged) and the number of Black Cleaver damaging hits h landed on participants[2] within the fight window. Both live outside the evidence tree this runbook permits.

conclusion: The 33.0 decrease is reproducible from the cached sources under either of the two mechanisms this scenario's name implicates, and under both of them the post-change number is the source-faithful one: the wiki's {{rd|8%|5%}} makes 8% wrong for a ranged Bloodsong holder, and math-foundations §2.3 makes the 0.8*max_stacks Black Cleaver constant an admitted approximation of the exact Cesàro mean C − C(C−1)/(2h), an identity I re-derived and confirmed. The old value 4074.9 is consistent only with the un-corrected reading in each case. Verdict: new_value_correct, at moderate confidence, with the scope limitation above stated plainly rather than papered over.
